<Route path="/ade/dashboard/versions" />

The **Overlays** tab on **Versions** is the overlay manager. A version's overlays are a stored,
ordered chain of [OpenAPI Overlay](../bring-in/overlays.md) 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 documents. They change
what the version **exports and publishes** (public descriptions, a partner's servers, `x-`
extensions) and leave the version itself unchanged. In the tab you can:

- write an overlay in the app, with **Update**, **Remove**, **Copy** and **Reusable** actions;
- preview it, with the number of values each action's target matches and every change before and
  after;
- **apply** the chain as a new version, or **export** the version with the chain applied.

Overlays modify OpenAPI documents, so the tab works on versions imported from OpenAPI or Swagger.

<Screenshot id="overlays-list" alt="The Overlays tab: one stored overlay with New overlay, Upload overlay, Preview, Apply as version and Export with overlays, then the preview's action table with a match count per action and the before and after table" />

## The chain

1. Open **Versions**, pick the project and **click the “Overlays” tab**.
2. Pick the **Revision**. Each overlay is listed in the order it applies, with its number of actions,
   its `sha256:` fingerprint and where it came from: **Uploaded**, **Export Studio**,
   **Agent enrichment** or **Lint fix**.
3. On a draft revision:
   - **Click “New overlay”** to write one (see below);
   - **click “Upload overlay”** to add overlay files (`.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json`, up to 1 MB each);
   - **click the pencil** on a row to edit that overlay;
   - **click ×** on a row to remove it.

A revision holds at most 10 overlays. A published revision's chain is read-only: you can still
preview it, apply it as a version and export with it, but you cannot change it.

## Write an overlay

**Click “New overlay”** (or the pencil on a stored overlay) to open the editor.

1. Enter a **Name** (how the chain lists it) and a **Title** (the document's `info.title`).
2. Choose the **Overlay version**. New overlays start at **1.1.0**, the first version with `copy`.
3. For each action, choose what it does and enter a JSONPath **Target**, which selects the values to
   change:

   | Action | What it does | Needs |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | **Update** | Merges the **Value (JSON)** into each match. Objects merge, and any other value replaces. | 1.0 |
   | **Remove** | Removes every match. | 1.0 |
   | **Copy** | Merges the value at **Copy from** into each match. **Copy from** must select exactly one value. | 1.1 |
   | **Reusable** | Runs an action the overlay declares under `components.actions`, on this target. | 1.2 |

   **Click “Add action”** for another one. The arrows reorder actions, and the bin deletes one.
   Actions apply top to bottom.
4. **Click “Preview”.** Apiome renders the revision with its chain and this unsaved overlay. When you
   edit an overlay, it previews in that overlay's place. A new overlay previews after the chain.
   - Each action shows how many values its target matched: **1 match**, **3 matches**,
     **No match** (the target selects nothing, so the action changes nothing) or **Not applied**
     (the action was refused, and the message under it says why).
   - **Before and after** lists every value the preview changes: its JSON Pointer, the value in the
     revision, the value after the overlays (**—** when there is none), and the overlay action
     that changed it.
5. **Click “Save overlay”.** Nothing is stored before this. Saving an edit replaces the overlay in
   place, at the same position.

If you change a field after previewing, the editor says **Edited since this preview**. Preview
again to see the current changes.

**Edit as → JSON** shows the whole Overlay document. Use it for anything the form does not cover,
such as `extends`, `components.actions` (the reusable actions) or `x-` extensions. The form keeps
those keys when you switch back.

<Screenshot id="overlay-preview" alt="The New overlay editor after Preview: Update, Remove and Copy actions each showing 1 match, then the before and after table naming the action that changed each value" />

### Example

This overlay retitles the API for partners, drops the internal server and copies the partner
defaults onto one operation:

| # | Action | Target | Value / Copy from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Update** | `$.info` | `{"title": "Pets for Partners"}` |
| 2 | **Remove** | `$.servers[0]` | |
| 3 | **Copy** | `$.paths['/pets'].get` | `$['x-partner-defaults']` |

## Preview the chain

**Click “Preview”** under the chain to render the whole chain the way an export does. It shows:

- the source and resolved fingerprints;
- **Actions and matches**: every action of every overlay, with its match count;
- **Before and after**: every changed value, with the action that changed it (its provenance). When
  several actions change one value, they are listed in order and the last one wins;
- any findings, such as `overlay.unmatched-target`, and the full change ledger.

## Apply as a version

Overlays normally apply only at export and publish. To make their changes part of a version:

1. **Click “Apply as version”.**
2. Enter a **New version label**, or leave it empty for a date and time label. A label the
   project already uses is refused.
3. **Click “Apply as version”** in the dialog.

Apiome imports the rendered document, exactly what **Preview** shows, as a new version of the
project. It runs the workspace's import quality gate first, as an upload would. The revision you
applied from keeps its overlays. The new version starts with an empty chain, because the changes
are now part of its source. Apply is refused when the chain is empty or changes nothing.

You need permission to import into the project and to edit it.

## Export with overlays

**Click “Export with overlays”** to open [Export studio](../ship/export-studio.mdx) on this
revision. Every export of the revision applies its chain, unless you switch **Apply stored overlays**
off in the Studio's **Overlays** step.

## REST API

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET …/overlays` | The chain. |
| `POST …/overlays` · `PUT …/overlays/{id}` · `DELETE …/overlays/{id}` | Add, replace or remove an overlay (draft revisions only). |
| `GET …/overlays/preview` | Render the chain. `report.actions` has a match count per action, and `diff` has the before and after rows. |
| `POST …/overlays/preview` | Render with an unsaved `draft` overlay, appended or in place of `replace_overlay_id`. Nothing is written. |
| `POST …/overlays/apply` | Import the rendered document as a new version (`version_label` optional). |

The prefix is `/v1/versions/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/{version_record_id}`. See the
[versions reference](/reference/rest/versions#apply-version-overlays-v1-versions-tenant-slug-project-id-version-record-id-overlays-apply-post).
Refusals carry a `code`:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `overlay-version-published` (409) | A write on a published revision. |
| `overlay-chain-full` (409) | The chain already holds 10 overlays. |
| `overlay-chain-empty` (409) | Apply on a revision with no overlays. |
| `overlay-no-changes` (409) | Apply when the chain changes nothing. |
| `version-exists` (409) | The new version label is taken. |
| `overlay-apply-import-failed` (422) | The rendered document could not be imported. |
